## What's new

Threadnote 5.0.0 turns working context into a verifiable lifecycle across agents, from reviewed closeout to health checks, CI, procedures, and private value reports.

### Resumable one-command setup

`threadnote setup <surface>` now previews one deterministic local setup plan; `--apply` initializes the core, current
repository manifest and seed, selected catalog integration and declared hooks, current code graph, doctor checks, and a
final source-backed Context Brief. A strict private `SetupReceiptV1` records only hashes, bounded operation state, and
recovery references, so interrupted plans resume safely and an unchanged completed apply is a no-op. `--undo` previews
receipt-owned rollback and `--undo --apply` removes only unchanged setup-created artifacts. Organization, composer, and
team-sharing setup remain outside this local workflow. Private value reports count applied setup starts, failures,
completions, supported-agent reuse, and bounded time to the verified Context Brief without recording tasks or paths.

### Project guidance import and projection

`threadnote guidance import <surface> --project <name>` previews existing adapter-declared project guidance and, with
`--apply`, creates or reuses a private Knowledge Delta candidate for review; it never approves or publishes. Approved
active durable memories can be explicitly projected with `threadnote guidance project ... --memory <uri>`, using
deterministic ordering plus a provenance- and hash-managed block. Status reports current, missing, modified, stale,
and evidence-unavailable targets, while preview-first removal preserves unmanaged content. Project-guidance support
now extends beyond the initial four surfaces and is declared by the canonical agent catalog, which reports each managed
target or an explicit unsupported reason. Shared physical targets use one target-owned receipt. Projection drift feeds
context health and Context Check. A second agent surface can reuse the same approved knowledge without separate
canonical copies.

### Reviewable health repairs and Git proposals

`threadnote context repair preview` now turns the bounded health report into deterministic, content-hash-bound repair
proposals without changing memory. `context repair apply` requires the exact proposal ID and revision plus `--approved`,
rechecks project and record preconditions, and uses a private recovery journal for safe retries. Automatic mutations are
limited to personal lifecycle-safe archives and exact removal of relations to direct personal URIs proven missing or
inactive; shared targets, stable identity aliases, ambiguous findings, citation repairs, guidance, preferences, and
smoke findings stay review-only. Equivalent preview/apply MCP tools preserve the same read-only versus destructive
boundary.

Applied durable Knowledge Delta candidates can be exported with `threadnote share propose` or the read-only
`share_propose` MCP tool. The canonical provider-neutral artifact binds the review revision, exact Git base, approved
source hashes, configured team, portable remote repository identity, and absent-or-exact target CAS while preserving
portable relations and stable shared identity. Export does not create a branch, commit, pull request, provider object,
or network request; `--output` is an explicit local-only write.

Provider-neutral local materialization remains preview-first. Its explicit apply path rechecks the repository, base,
proposal, and target CAS bindings before creating the deterministic branch and commit, reuses an idempotent retry, and
never pushes, opens a pull request, or calls a hosted provider.

### Agent integration catalog

`threadnote agents list --json` now reports a catalog of 27 agent surfaces with setup guidance, capability boundaries,
platform coverage, and verification metadata. Managed integrations can be previewed, installed, repaired, inspected, and
removed through one lifecycle. New managed user-scope paths include Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Amp, and Factory Droid;
catalog-only and partial entries stay clearly marked instead of being presented as fully managed.

### Fair multi-worktree graph scheduling

Concurrent code-graph builds now share a home-wide two-builder budget with checkout-aware scheduling, so one checkout is
less likely to occupy every build slot while another waits. Interactive requests retain priority, background work ages
into the same priority tier after a bounded wait, and live pre-5.0 builders continue to count safely during upgrades.

Build status, JSON output, and MCP progress now expose bounded queue position, admission class, active resource, blocker,
and cumulative phase and wait durations. This makes graph-readiness delays attributable without exposing repository
paths or source content. Materialization timing keeps scheduler admission wait separate from active attribution work,
so performance regressions remain actionable.

Ordinary MCP query, node, neighbors, and explain calls can continue immediately from an immutable compatible stale ready
snapshot while a durable refresh is active, queued, or deferred. Privacy-safe continuity reports opaque `cgdq_` tokens
and bounded retry guidance; path, impact, whole-graph analysis, and exact-current citations remain strict. Agents can
continue bounded discovery and verify exact source literals without tight polling. Durable latest-wins reduction,
irrevocable publication, and crash recovery converge to the newest demand.

### Lifecycle and closeout foundations

Memory schema v5 adds optional ownership and `review_after` maintenance metadata. Bounded Knowledge Deltas and
`threadnote closeout preview/apply` make proposed context changes reviewable before they become durable knowledge.

`threadnote context health` reports stale citations, review dates, broken relations, duplicates, and pending conflicts in
text or JSON without mutating memory. `threadnote context check` scopes those findings to changed files and provides stable
text, JSON, and SARIF results for CI.

### Verified procedures and private value reports

Procedure manifests can be verified against exact artifacts and fixtures, then inspected as current, incompatible,
locally modified, unverified, or update-available. Verification is preview-first and never executes downloaded procedures
automatically. Manifest v2 adds bounded discovery metadata plus deterministic stable/preview rollout policy while v1
remains readable for local verification and status.
Exact current manifest, receipt, and strict BOM-free, NUL-free UTF-8 artifact text can be previewed and explicitly published to a
configured Git share; same-version conflicts fail closed and unrelated worktree or staged files remain untouched.
Context Brief admits a bounded task-relevant dependency closure through the public agent catalog, chooses the highest
cohort-admitted semantic version, and exposes distinct Git-share provenance without artifact bodies or executable
commands. Procedure-bearing Context Briefs use response/projector schema v4 and agent-view schema v2; older versions
reject the new field, while unavailable, truncated, or conflicting repository evidence remains an explicit coverage gap.
CLI and MCP publication share the same preview-ID, explicit-approval boundary; pushing remains separately explicit.
The MCP adapters live in the full toolset, preserving the bounded default core schema budget.

`threadnote value report` summarizes the local task-context loop using content-free counts. Its explicit export remains
preview-first and redacted: it excludes queries, memory text, source code, paths, repository names, and stable user IDs.

Recall results now surface `useful`, `wrong`, `pin`, `dismiss`, and distinct `applied` feedback in MCP, CLI guidance,
and Manager; applied means the context materially informed a plan or change. ValueReportV1 remains backward-readable
while adding applied counts/rates, and Manager presents activation, first-evidence timing, second-agent reuse, Knowledge
Delta outcomes, and health resolution. Preview-first retention and category-scoped deletion cover local feedback, value
events, and explicit redacted export bundles without adding any background upload.

### Provider-neutral graph machine credentials

Graph and OCI machine helpers now support explicit OAuth 2.0 client-credentials configuration, including Okta custom
authorization servers with path-based issuers, HTTP Basic client authentication, and `cid`/`scp` claims. Generic helper
commands and environment names retain safe Auth0 aliases. Explicit same-origin token/JWKS endpoints and an optional
audience request parameter preserve exact authority, scope, and ten-minute lifetime validation. Publisher preflight and
container wiring use the same provider-neutral contract.
